newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen authorities deny report Basayev attacked.
newsitem.headline: Chechen authorities deny report Basayev attacked.

text.p: Chechen interior ministry officials denied reports on Monday of a bomb attack against guerrilla commander Shamil Basayev, who was runner-up in the breakaway Russian region's presidential election in January.

"There was no bomb explosion," an official told Reuters in Grozny. He added that a small quantity of explosive, possibly rifle rounds, had, however, detonated on Sunday some 250 metres (yards) from Basayev's headquarters in the regional capital.

Chechen television said on Sunday night that the 32-year-old Basayev, who made himself Russia's public enemy number one with a raid on the town of Budennovsk in 1995, had escaped unharmed when a radio controlled device went off as his motorcade passed.
Itar-Tass news agency on Monday quoted Chechen interior ministry officials saying a radio-controlled mine exploded in southern Grozny on Sunday afternoon as Basayev's cars went by.
It said a guard was injured, but Basayev was not hurt.
Basayev himself was not immediately available for comment on the reports, which could not otherwise be checked.

Aslan Maskhadov, the guerrilla leader who beat Basayev to the presidency, has promised to restore law and order after two years of war against Russian troops. But Chechnya is awash with weapons and security remains a worry for many.
Four Russian journalists were kidnapped last week and an Italian photographer was still missing on Monday after being seized by armed men two weeks ago.
Tass quoted Chechen officials saying an unnamed Italian government representative arrived in Grozny on Monday to conduct negotiations to secure the release of Mauro Galligani, 55.
It also quoted officials saying the four Russians appeared to be still alive.
